misconceptions.description: Treating peer review as encouragement or surface praise rather than a check on whether the conclusion is supported by the evidence
misconceptions.trigger: reviewer offers approval or style comments instead of testing the reasoning
misconceptions.feedback: Check whether the brief's conclusion follows from its own evidence and name the exact gap. Praise and style notes do not strengthen the reasoning.

misconceptions.description: Reviewing a brief by stating which tool or approach the reviewer would have chosen rather than assessing the author's reasoning
misconceptions.trigger: reviewer rewrites the decision in their own image
misconceptions.feedback: Review the author's reasoning against their own question and evidence, not the brief you would have written.

misconceptions.description: Forwarding an AI-generated review as your own without reading the brief and verifying the points
misconceptions.trigger: reviewer passes on AI feedback without checking it against the brief
misconceptions.feedback: Read the brief yourself and use AI points as prompts. Only pass on critiques you have verified against the brief's actual evidence.

misconceptions.description: Responding to a peer review flag by asserting confidence rather than supplying evidence or revising the claim
misconceptions.trigger: author dismisses a gap because they feel sure of the conclusion
misconceptions.feedback: Confidence is not evidence. Add the missing support or revise the conclusion to match what the evidence shows.
